hints: Look closely at the walls in the photomicrograph. Which vessel, P or Q, has the much thicker, darker muscular wall and narrow lumen?
Remember the flow sequence: arteries lead into arterioles, while venules drain into larger veins. Match the thick-walled and thin-walled vessel to its correct sequence.
walkthrough:
**Compare the walls of P and Q**

Look at the image side by side. Vessel Q in the centre has a thick, dense wall with smooth muscle and a small, rounded lumen. Vessel P on the outside has a much thinner wall and a wider, flatter lumen.

Rule to remember: thick wall plus small lumen = artery, thin wall plus wide lumen = vein.

**Link structure to position in the network**

Arteries carry high pressure blood away from the heart, so they need thick elastic and muscle walls. They branch into smaller arterioles, then capillaries. Veins carry low pressure blood back to the heart, so they are thin walled. They are formed when tiny venules join together.

So: artery carries blood into arterioles, vein carries blood from venules.

**Identify P and Q and choose the row**

Q is the artery, so Q carries blood into arterioles. P is the vein, so P carries blood from venules. That combination is P = from venules, Q = into arterioles.

options.A: Incorrect, as P is a thin-walled vein, not an artery, so it cannot carry blood into arterioles.
options.B: Incorrect, as it reverses both vessels. P is a vein and Q is an artery.
options.C: Correct. P has a thin wall and wide lumen so is a vein collecting blood from venules, and Q has a thick wall so is an artery feeding blood into arterioles.
options.D: Incorrect, as Q is a thick-walled artery, not a vein, so it does not carry blood from venules.
